steps.body: Ten is the easiest number to add to. To add across ten, first use part of the second number to fill a ten.
steps.narration: Ten is the easiest number to add to. To add across ten, first use part of the second number to fill a ten.

widget.prompt: The frame holds 8. Fill it to ten.

commonCounts.feedback: That adds only one. A frame of 8 needs 2 more to reach ten.
That counts the dots you added rather than the full frame. The frame should show 10 in all.

widget.missFeedback: Count the dots already there, then add just enough to reach 10.
widget.successFeedback: 8 and 2 more makes ten — the frame is full.

predict.prompt: The frame holds 8 and you have 5 more dots. How many will it take to fill the frame to ten?
predict.reveal: 8 needs just 2 to reach ten. The other 3 stay outside, making 13 in all.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2f make ten.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for g2f make ten must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines g2f make ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: Breaking 5 into 2 and 3 turns a hard fact into a ten-plus fact.

commonErrors.feedback: That stops at ten. After using 2 to make ten, 3 still remain to add.
That stops one short. 8 + 2 = 10, then 3 more makes 13.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Split 5 into the part that completes ten and the part left over.
widget.successFeedback: Correct — 8 + 2 makes ten, then 3 more gives 13.
